audits.resolution_reason: Emitted foreground fixed to1 makes replace-all-non1-by8 indistinguishable throughout generator alphabet, but loses colors on five of six canonical outputs. Domain restriction and dead anchor_corner control; not an incorrectly labelled generated sample.
audits.text:
## 1bd5f3eafb8e

**Finding: foreground-color collapse leaves a concrete teaching shortcut unrefutable on the entire emitted domain.** The selected Racket rule crops the half identified by the two markers and recolors only color 5 to 8. The generator initializes color 8, writes foreground color 1, and writes marker color 5 in every ordinary and degenerate branch. Consequently the rival “perform the same marker-directed crop, then replace every non-1 cell with 8” agrees on every grid this source can emit. It erases legitimate foreground colors in the selected canonical task. This equivalence follows from the source alphabet, rather than from extrapolating a finite sampling sweep.

The documented domain explicitly says “bg=8 with 1s,” so this is a teaching-domain restriction, **not** an incorrectly labeled emitted example or a claim that arbitrary colors belong to that documented domain. The task's own canonical pairs provide the larger-domain witnesses: five of six use foreground colors other than 1. Actual public Racket application exactly reproduced all six canonical outputs; the rival disagreed on those five, changing 16, 25, 9, 2, and 24 cells respectively. In particular `canonical-train-1` outputs a 10×10 grid with colors 7 and 8, while the rival outputs an all-8 grid. The two generated grids in this bounded probe agree with the rival and pass `self_check`.

| Probe | Actual public output colors | Rival mismatching cells |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| canonical-train-0 | 1, 8 | 0 |
| canonical-train-1 | 7, 8 | 16 |
| canonical-train-2 | 3, 8 | 25 |
| canonical-train-3 | 4, 8 | 9 |
| canonical-test-0 | 8, 9 | 2 |
| canonical-test-1 | 2, 8 | 24 |
| generated-anchor-False | 1, 8 | 0 |
| generated-anchor-True | 1, 8 | 0 |

**Additional concrete control defect:** `AXES` advertises `anchor_corner` as a boolean control, but generation never reads it. Paired calls with seed 17, sample index 0, difficulty `easy`, and overrides `grid_h=10`, `grid_w=10`, `ones_pattern="scattered"`, `ones_density=0.25`, `marker_orientation="horizontal_split"`, `marker_side="bottom_or_right"`, and `anchor_corner=false` versus `true` produced identical inputs and identical actual public Racket outputs. Both markers are in column 5, at rows 5 and 7; both checks return `[]`. The paired measurement confirms the no-op, and inspection establishes that the control is ignored for all calls. Its intended anchoring behavior is not specified more precisely, so no additional semantics are inferred.

Recommended follow-up: add foreground-color variation covering the canonical palette and ensure a generated teaching witness forces retention of a non-1 foreground color. Keep marker/background colors distinct and pin the selected rule while verifying new draws through public Racket. Either implement and document `anchor_corner` or remove the advertised axis. This audit did not modify source.

**Evidence and scope:** [checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/summary.json](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/summary.json) retains every exact input, rival output, actual public Racket output, canonical identity or generator replay arguments, and `self_check` result. [input.json](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/input.json) contains the bare eight-input apply payload; [racket.json](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/racket.json) is the genuine public apply receipt. [canonical-pairs.json](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/canonical-pairs.json), [catalog.json](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/catalog.json), and [canonical-rule.rkt](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/canonical-rule.rkt) retain the portable authoring data and selected rule. [prepare.py](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/prepare.py) uses public `Catalog.get` and portable `reviewer_support.canonical_pairs/find_root`; no private runner APIs were imported. [finalize.py](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/finalize.py) binds the audited source to the actual apply receipt and verifies all six canonical labels. There were eight actual Racket cases, zero Racket errors, six exact canonical agreements, five canonical rival disagreements, and two generated rival agreements. All eight `self_check` calls returned `[]`.

Audited generator SHA-256: `c9ea94fcfa1acac8a2f7a4429fd3e17d311b2bfa506d227cc7a4ce14f7908f0a`. Selected/catalog/executed normalized rule hash: `102be25765ff`. Raw program-solution SHA-256: `c48a8d13f890f19399457fefd7478704cb35a6add2d26d304729a3eeffa37322`. The actual receipt's runtime callable-text SHA-256 is `34fabd77b82e42082b4f3ce426fed172b3dc69da0eef01f9008eb56754f6dbf6`; this hashes a different representation and is not substituted for the raw rule hash.

Unique command receipts are `checks/commands/audit-1bd5f3eafb8e-{prepare,cases,public-apply,finalize}.{json,log}`. Their generic `source_before/source_after` fields stamp the main assigned task, not this audit target. The target-specific binding above is explicitly retained in [probe.json](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/probe.json), [summary.json](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/summary.json), and the public [racket.json](checks/audit/1bd5f3eafb8e/racket.json) receipt. This was a single bounded audit of the once-drawn target after the main repair. No reroll, other-target investigation, source edits, or earlier-round measurements were used. It does not establish lesson-level shortcut prevalence across an independently measured production census or exhaustively test every override.
